Broward County Florida Inmate Lookup

If you need to locate someone in the Broward County jail system, there are several official resources available to help you find current inmate information. A broward county florida inmate lookup can be completed quickly through the Broward County Sheriff's Office or the Florida Department of Corrections. Understanding how to search these databases and what information you'll need can save you time and help you get answers faster.

How to Search Broward County Jail Records

  1. Visit the Broward County Sheriff's Office official inmate search portal or use the search tools provided on their website.
  2. Enter the inmate's full name or booking number if you have it. First and last name are typically required fields.
  3. Review the search results, which will display the inmate's current location, booking date, charges, and bond information.
  4. If the person is not found in the county jail, check the Florida Department of Corrections inmate locator for those serving state sentences.
  5. For federal charges, search the Federal Bureau of Prisons inmate locator database to confirm if the person is in federal custody.
  6. Take note of the booking number and facility location, as this information will be needed for visitation requests, phone calls, or money transfers.
  7. If you need additional details such as court records or case information, contact the Broward County Court Records office directly.

Bail Bond Information for Broward County

When someone is arrested in Broward County, bail may be set during their first appearance or arraignment. Many families choose to work with bail bondsmen to secure release from custody. A typical bail bondsman charges a non-refundable fee of 10 percent of the total bail amount set by the judge. This fee is the cost for the bondsman to post the full bail with the court on behalf of the defendant. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, the bondsman's fee would be $1,000, and the defendant would only need to pay this amount rather than the full bail to be released.

The arraignment typically occurs within 24 to 72 hours of arrest in Broward County. During this hearing, the judge reviews the charges and sets bail or bond conditions. If bail is unaffordable or the defendant cannot secure a bondsman, they may request a bond reduction or ask the court to release them on their own recognizance. It is important to have bail bond information readily available, as delays in securing a bondsman can result in extended time in custody. Licensed bail bondsmen in Broward County are available 24 hours a day to process bond agreements quickly.

Visitation Rules at Broward County Jail

  • Visitation Hours: General visitation is typically available on weekends and certain weekday evenings; check the specific facility for exact times.
  • Valid Identification: All visitors must present a valid government-issued ID such as a driver's license or passport.
  • Dress Code: Visitors are prohibited from wearing certain clothing including tank tops, transparent garments, short skirts, and clothing with offensive language or imagery.
  • Video Visitation: Remote video visits are available through the jail's approved video visitation system for added convenience and flexibility.
  • Children Policy: Children under 18 are permitted but must be supervised by an adult at all times during visits.
  • No Contraband: Personal items, money, or any prohibited materials cannot be brought into the facility during in-person visits.
  • Advance Registration: Some facilities require advance registration or scheduling of visits, so contact the jail ahead of time to confirm requirements.

What to Expect After Arrest in Broward County

  1. Booking: The arrestee is brought to the Broward County jail facility where personal information, photographs, and fingerprints are recorded in the system.
  2. Medical Screening: A medical evaluation is conducted to assess the inmate's health status and identify any existing medical conditions or medications needed.
  3. Classification: The inmate is assigned a security classification and housing assignment based on the nature of charges, criminal history, and behavior assessment.
  4. Arraignment: The inmate appears before a judge, usually within 24 to 72 hours, where charges are read and bail or bond is set.
  5. Transfer: If the inmate is sentenced to state prison, they may be transferred to a Florida Department of Corrections facility to serve their sentence.

How to Contact Broward County Jail

For general inquiries about an inmate, visitation policies, or facility information, you can contact Broward County Jail directly. The main phone line and website provide access to inmate search tools and staff who can answer questions about custody status and facility procedures. Having the inmate's full name, date of birth, or booking number on hand will help staff locate the correct individual quickly.
